column1: Bajaj's electric Chetak factory is making barely half the scooters it made a year earlier.
One small magnet... and most of them come from China.
A year earlier, about twenty thousand Chetaks a month.
This July... less than eleven thousand.
The raw material for that magnet is lying in the sand on our own beaches — in Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha.
By our own government's count, India's sands hold about seven million tonnes of rare earths.
So why can't India make the magnet?
Stay with me, and you'll see three things.
The hard step nobody else wanted to do.
Then, about five minutes in, the secret inside our sand that kept it locked away.
And at the end, the date you should watch.
